headline: Beyond the Pitch: Messi builds football club empire for post-retirement life
summary: The 39-year-old superstar is acquiring clubs in Spain and Uruguay, focusing on youth development rather than coaching.
details: Lionel Messi is preparing for life after professional football by building a network of club ownerships. The superstar has recently completed the acquisition of Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense and already owns the Catalan fifth-tier side UE Cornella.
caption:
No coaching, just ownership. Lionel Messi is building a football empire for his second act.

Lionel Messi is preparing for life after professional football by building a network of club ownerships. The superstar has recently completed the acquisition of Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense and already owns the Catalan fifth-tier side UE Cornella.

headline: Cristiano Ronaldo accuses coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises
summary: The Portuguese star claims he left the national team camp after the coach failed to honor agreements regarding his playing time and public statements.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has issued a lengthy statement accusing Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word twice, leading to his departure from the team camp in Copenhagen.
The dispute began when Ronaldo claimed Jesus agreed he would miss the Norway and Denmark matches to manage his fitness, but then told him he would play for 30 minutes on the day of the Norway game.
Ronaldo stated that despite warming up from halftime onwards, he was never called into the match, which he described as a mistake by the coach.
A subsequent meeting involving Al Nassr's sporting director produced an eight-point document where Jesus allegedly agreed to clarify the events at a press conference.
Ronaldo claims the coach's public remarks did not match their private discussion, prompting the forward to leave the camp without waiting for further promises.
Coach Jorge Jesus has denied making any such agreement with the player, though he noted that the door remains open for Ronaldo's return.
Ronaldo apologized for failing to greet supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates, acknowledging that his role as captain makes his conduct more serious.
The forward has called for the Portuguese Football Federation to assess and punish his actions, while insisting he remains available to compete for the national team once any suspension is served.
caption:
Broken promises and a camp exit. Cristiano Ronaldo claims coach Jorge Jesus betrayed his trust twice.

Cristiano Ronaldo has issued a lengthy statement accusing Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word twice, leading to his departure from the team camp in Copenhagen.

The dispute began when Ronaldo claimed Jesus agreed he would miss the Norway and Denmark matches to manage his fitness, but then told him he would play for 30 minutes on the day of the Norway game.

Ronaldo stated that despite warming up from halftime onwards, he was never called into the match, which he described as a mistake by the coach.

A subsequent meeting involving Al Nassr's sporting director produced an eight-point document where Jesus allegedly agreed to clarify the events at a press conference.

Ronaldo claims the coach's public remarks did not match their private discussion, prompting the forward to leave the camp without waiting for further promises.

Coach Jorge Jesus has denied making any such agreement with the player, though he noted that the door remains open for Ronaldo's return.

Ronaldo apologized for failing to greet supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates, acknowledging that his role as captain makes his conduct more serious.

The forward has called for the Portuguese Football Federation to assess and punish his actions, while insisting he remains available to compete for the national team once any suspension is served.
